recent_articles.title: ED raids Pinarayi Vijayan's residences in CMRL-Exalogic case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Enforcement Directorate (ED)** conducted raids on the residences of former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his daughter, T. Veena, in Kannur and Thiruvananthapuram, alleging that her defunct firm received substantial monthly retainers from **Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL)** between 2017 and 2021 without rendering any tangible service. The raids triggered protests across the state, with CPI(M) activists allegedly vandalizing vehicles carrying ED officials.  The ED is verifying bank transactions of Ms. Veena while stating no incriminating documents were found at Mr. Vijayan's residence.

recent_articles.title: ED freezes ₹18.36 crore and 242 bank accounts Exalogic-CMRL payoff case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **ED** froze ₹18.36 crore in 242 accounts following raids conducted on Wednesday as part of an alleged pay-off case involving **T. Veena**, daughter of Kerala's Leader of the Opposition, **Pinarayi Vijayan**. The searches targeted premises linked to Ms. Veena and the management of the **CMRL** (Kannur Metro Rail Limited) in Kerala and Bengaluru.  The ED is investigating proceeds of crime generated by the CMRL, led by S.N. Sasidharan Kartha, along with Ms. Veena. The investigation stems from previous findings by the Income Tax department that revealed fake expenses amounting to ₹130 crore.

recent_articles.title: Defiant Pinarayi Vijayan raises fist after ED raid, vows ‘long battle’ against BJP and Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pinarayi Vijayan**, former Kerala Chief Minister and now Leader of the Opposition, emerged from his residence in Thiruvananthapuram to greet hundreds of **CPI(M)** workers protesting against a seven-hour raid by the **Enforcement Directorate (ED)**.  He criticized the BJP for using central enforcement agencies to target opposition figures while accusing the Congress of tacitly supporting these actions.  **Mr. Vijayan** asserted that the Communist movement would not be deterred and vowed to fight for democracy and equality, despite the damage caused to vehicles by protesting party workers who were subsequently arrested.

recent_articles.title: ED raids former Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan’s houses in CMRL pay-off case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Enforcement Directorate (ED)** conducted raids on the homes of former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his family, along with other locations across the state, in connection with an investigation into alleged political payoffs. The ED's action followed a High Court order allowing them to investigate **Exalogic**, a firm owned by Vijayan's daughter, T. Veena, which allegedly received monthly retainers from **Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL)** during the 2017-2021 period without providing tangible services. The ED is investigating whether these payments constituted money laundering.

recent_articles.title: Assault on Youth Congress workers in Alappuzha: SIT says 'assault unlawful’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A Special Investigation Team (SIT) concluded that the assault on Indian Youth Congress activists in Alappuzha by police officers, including those from former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan's security detail, was unlawful. The SIT recommended criminal charges against the involved officers and found procedural irregularities in the initial investigation. **Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala** will review the report before forwarding it to the Home Secretary for further action.

recent_articles.title: ‘Needless fuss’: Kerala CM V.D. Satheesan defends posting former State poll chief Rathan Kelkar as his Secretary - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan** stated that the appointment of **Rathan U. Kelkar**, former Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala), as his Secretary was not a cause for concern and dismissed criticisms from the opposition.  He emphasized that no political party in Kerala had accused Mr. Kelkar of election manipulation, noting that he was appointed by the previous CPI(M)-led LDF government. **Mr. Satheesan** further highlighted that Mr. Kelkar's appointment is not comparable to similar controversies in West Bengal where allegations against the CEO were made.

recent_articles.title: Pinarayi flays crackdown on Cockroach Janta Party - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pinarayi Vijayan**, leader of the Opposition, criticized the **Union government's** withholding of the **Cockroach Janta Party’s X handle**. He argued that this action reflects intolerance towards democratic protests and suggests fear of the youth movement becoming a political force.  Vijayan stated that the platform has gained significant traction due to its focus on addressing unemployment and inequality, highlighting the deep discontent among young people.

recent_articles.title: Congress leader Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan elected Kerala Speaker - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan**, a senior Congress leader, was elected as the Speaker of the 16th Kerala Legislative Assembly on Friday (May 22, 2026). He won with 101 votes, defeating **A.C. Moideen** and **B.B. Gopakumar**.  The election took place after **G. Sudhakaran**, the previous Pro Tem Speaker, chose not to vote.  **V.D. Satheesan**, the Chief Minister, and **Pinarayi Vijayan**, the Leader of the Opposition, led Radhakrishnan to the Speaker's chair.

recent_articles.title: ASHAs meet Kerala CM-designate V.D. Satheesan, urge him to honour pre-poll promises - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala ASHA Health Workers’ Association (KAHWA)** met with **V.D. Satheesan**, the new Chief Minister-designate, to reiterate their demands for an increase in honorarium and retirement benefits. They expressed hope that the new government would prioritize addressing their concerns.  **Satheesan** assured them that he would not forget his pre-election promise of resolving their grievances.

recent_articles.title: Watch: Congress ends suspense: V. D. Satheesan to be next Kerala CM | Above the Fold | 14.05.2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala Congress** named V.D. Satheesan as its new Chief Minister after weeks of internal discussions, ending months of uncertainty.  The **BRICS Foreign Ministers’ meeting**, hosted by India in New Delhi, saw **External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar** address key global challenges and diplomatic priorities.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM announcement LIVE: Congress names V.D. Satheesan as Kerala CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **AICC** announced **V.D. Satheesan** as the Chief Minister designate of Kerala, ending a ten-day period of uncertainty following the May 4th election results. The announcement was made by **Ajay Maken**, **Mukul Wasnik**, and **Deepa Dasmunshi** at the AICC Office.  The Congress will now proceed to form the government in the state after securing the majority.

recent_articles.title: CPI(M) defends Vijayan, says leadership is collective after Kerala defeat - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **M.A. Baby**, **CPI(M)** general secretary, stated that **Pinarayi Vijayan** cannot be solely held responsible for the Left Democratic Front's (LDF) loss in Kerala. He emphasized that the party functions as a collective unit and that **Vijayan** led the campaign as its senior-most member.  Baby did not specify who within the LDF will assume the Leader of the Opposition position, despite widespread speculation about **Vijayan** potentially holding it.

recent_articles.title: Kerala’s fiscal worries - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, the **Kerala** Opposition Leader, claims that the newly elected **UDF** government inherited a nearly empty treasury from the **LDF**.  The new government faces challenges in managing Kerala's finances, including high expenditures on salaries, pensions, and interest payments, limited tax revenue potential, and the impact of the 16th Finance Commission awards. The outgoing Finance Minister, **K.N. Balagopal**, disputes these claims, emphasizing that the state is in a better financial position than it was under the previous government.  The new government will need to address these challenges to fulfill its promises of development and social welfare programs.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM debate: Kharge to hold crucial talks with senior leaders today evening - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, **AICC president**, will meet with key figures in the Kerala Congress leadership, including **K.C. Venugopal**, **V.D. Satheesan**, and **Ramesh Chennithala**, on Saturday (May 9, 2026) to discuss the selection of a new Chief Minister.  **Rahul Gandhi** is expected to meet with the Kerala leaders after a consensus emerges from the meeting chaired by **Kharge**.

recent_articles.title: Final decision on Kerala CM turns into political cliff-hanger as ball now in Congress High Command’s court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress** party in Kerala is facing uncertainty regarding the selection of its Chief Minister, with three potential candidates – **V.D. Satheesan**, **K.C. Venugopal**, and **Ramesh Chennithala** – vying for the position.  The decision appears to be pending a final announcement from the **Congress High Command**, who are reportedly meeting with the contenders in Delhi on Saturday.

recent_articles.title: Kerala election results: Congress high command to pick Kerala CM; most UDF allies for Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress Legislative Party** in Kerala authorized the party high command to choose the next Chief Minister after a resolution was passed.  **AICC** observers, **Mukul Wasnik**, **Ajay Maken**, and **Deepa Dasmunsi**, met with all 63 legislators to gauge their preferences for the position. The three frontrunners in the race are former Leader of Opposition **V.D. Satheesan**, **K.C. Venugopal**, and **Ramesh Chennithala**.  **UDF** allies, including the **IUML**, have indicated support for **Satheesan**, while **KPCC** president **Sunny Joseph** has called for a decision based on public sentiment. The observers will present their findings to the high command, who is expected to make a final call soon.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM to be chosen by Congress High Command is acceptable for CMP, says C.P. John - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **C. P. John**, general secretary of the **Communist Marxist Party (CMP)**, stated that the party would accept the **Congress High Command's** chosen Kerala Chief Minister.  He also acknowledged the possibility of a ministerial berth for the CMP but declined to comment further. **John** expressed gratitude to voters and noted the CMP's historical performance in Kannur despite a decline in its overall vote base. He emphasized addressing the potable water crisis in Thiruvananthapuram as his immediate priority.

recent_articles.title: ​Back in the saddle: On the Congress win in the Kerala Assembly polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress**-led **United Democratic Front (UDF)** won a landslide victory in the Kerala state assembly elections, ending 10 years of opposition. The UDF capitalized on anti-incumbency sentiment against the **CPI(M)**-led **Left Democratic Front (LDF)** and secured 102 seats.  The **BJP** made gains, securing three seats while drawing a substantial share of votes in various regions. The LDF faced criticism for its governance, with some accusing it of nepotism and overbearing leadership.

recent_articles.title: Kerala polls: Congress-led UDF won not due to any individual’s efforts but as people were fed up, says NSS general secretary - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **G. Sukumaran Nair**, general secretary of the **Nair Service Society (NSS)**, stated that the Congress-led UDF's victory in the 2026 Kerala Assembly polls was due to public dissatisfaction with the government and not individual efforts by anyone, including **V.D. Satheesan**.  **Mr. Nair** attributed the Left's loss to internal issues within the party, not anti-incumbency sentiment. While acknowledging differences with **Satheesan**, he emphasized that these were not used against him during the election and asserted that the NSS did not dictate support for any candidate.

recent_articles.title: Results signal political shift in Kannur, says Sunny Joseph - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **KPCC** president Sunny Joseph criticized the **CPI(M)**'s performance in the Payyannur Assembly election, calling it a "major setback" for the party. He attributed the loss to public discontent with the government and urged introspection from the leadership and cadre.  Joseph suggested that the developments could lead to further political shifts in the future.

recent_articles.title: What Modi’s big win in Indian state elections could mean for its democracy | Elections News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won the West Bengal state assembly elections, marking a significant victory for the party and raising concerns about potential authoritarianism. The BJP's win comes after a history of religious cleavages in the state, but also amidst accusations of voter suppression targeting Muslims.  Actor Joseph Vijay won the Tamil Nadu Assembly election, breaking a long-standing duopoly by the Dravidian parties. In Kerala, the Communist party lost to an alliance led by the Congress. The BJP's consolidation of power has grown with its victories in 21 out of 28 states, raising questions about India's future political landscape and democratic processes.

recent_articles.title: Assembly Election 2026 results LIVE: TN, Kerala, West Bengal head into Govt formation mode - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, **M.K. Stalin**, and **Pinarayi Vijayan** have lost their respective elections, paving the way for new governments in **Tamil Nadu**, **West Bengal**, and **Kerala**. The BJP secured a landslide victory in West Bengal, while **Vijay**'s TVK party emerged as the single-largest party in Tamil Nadu.  The saffron party also retained Assam and will be part of the incumbent NDA government in Puducherry.

recent_articles.title: What the winner must learn from the loser in Kerala: No leader is inevitable - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **United Democratic Front** won the Kerala state elections, defeating the **Communist Party of India (Marxist)-led Left Democratic Front**.  The UDF's victory highlights the voters' preference for collaborative leadership over a singular figurehead. The LDF campaign focused heavily on **Pinarayi Vijayan**, its sole face, while the UDF emphasized teamwork and unity among its leaders. This approach resonated with voters who felt the LDF had become too centralized under Vijayan's rule, leading to dissatisfaction within the party itself.

recent_articles.title: ​Lost and found: The Hindu Editorial on the 2026 Assembly elections - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 Assembly elections in Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry resulted in significant shifts in India's political landscape. The BJP secured victories in Assam and Puducherry while the Congress suffered its worst performance in Assam. In West Bengal, the BJP capitalized on long-term planning and a tainted election process to achieve a decisive victory.  The TVK led by actor C. Joseph Vijay made a historic debut in Tamil Nadu, becoming the first non-Dravidian Chief Minister. The Congress faces an internal challenge in Kerala with multiple candidates vying for the Chief Minister position. **Amit Shah**, Home Minister, is likely to gain further influence within the BJP as it continues its expansion across regions and social groups.  The results suggest a potential realignment of the Opposition, opening opportunities for the Congress to consolidate and galvanize support against the BJP.

recent_articles.title: India loses its last left-wing government after five decades | Politics News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: India's left-wing parties have lost their grip on power, with the **United Democratic Front** winning the Kerala state elections. This marks the first time in over half a century that no Indian state is ruled by the left. The decline of the left's influence is attributed to factors such as its inability to address issues like caste and gender inequality and its perceived lack of relevance in the face of changing economic realities. Experts suggest that while the left may not be in power, it remains an important opposition force capable of influencing policy debates.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Election Results 2026 LIVE: UDF leads in the State, CM Pinarayi Vijayan trails in Dharmadam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress-led UDF** is on track to secure a majority in the Kerala Assembly elections, with trends indicating they will surpass their target of 100 seats.  As counting progressed, the UDF held a commanding lead in over 100 constituencies while the **CPI(M)-led LDF** lagged behind in under 40. The **BJP-led NDA** secured only two seats according to early results.  Congress MLA Chandy Oommen won his constituency by a significant margin.

recent_articles.title: ​Primary league: On the Congress, UDF, 2026 Kerala Assembly elections - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders in Kerala have been caught off guard by the **IUML's** public endorsement of  **V.D. Satheesan** for Chief Minister, despite the party's internal agreements to let the legislature choose its leader. This move has sparked concerns about sectarian tensions and the IUML's maximalist demands within the UDF coalition, potentially jeopardizing the Front's social base. The **IUML**, however, is urged to respect established norms of Kerala's coalition politics, which involve a collective leadership decision by all partners.

recent_articles.title: This May Day reminds workers to be more organised, says Kerala Chief Minister - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala**'s trade union organizations and workers from various sectors celebrated May Day on Friday, expressing concerns over the erosion of labor rights and the introduction of four new labor codes. **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan**, in a Facebook post, acknowledged the growing strength of labor strikes across India despite neoliberal policies that undermine worker rights.  He urged workers to remain organized. The celebrations included rallies and public events in all 14 district centers and over 250 other locations. Trade unions like CITU, AITUC, AIUTUC, AICTU, SEWA, TUCI, HMS, NLC, INLC, HMKP, KTUCM, JTU, and NTU joined forces to mark the occasion.

recent_articles.title: UDF will probe “corruption” in the cancellation of DBFOO power supply contracts if it comes to power: V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, leader of the Opposition, called for a probe into alleged corruption behind the cancellation of long-term power supply contracts by the **Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission** and the **KSEB**. He argued that the decision to cancel these contracts led to unscheduled loadsheddings and increased power costs for the state.  The contracts had guaranteed power at ₹4.29 per unit, but the cancellation resulted in higher costs of ₹6 to ₹12 per unit, causing daily losses of ₹15 crore to ₹20 crore for the KSEB.

recent_articles.title: Fire accident in Kerala: Firecracker factory blast leaves 13 dead
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Thirteen** people were killed in a firecracker factory explosion in **Kerala**, India, on Tuesday. The incident occurred near paddy fields where workers were assembling fireworks for the upcoming Thrissur Pooram festival.  At least five individuals are reported to be in critical condition and rescue efforts have been hampered by secondary blasts and poor road access.  **K Gireesh Kumar**, secretary of the Tiruvambady temple committee, stated that the group had permission to store 2,000kg of firecrackers for each display. **Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** has announced financial assistance for the victims. The cause of the explosion is still under investigation.

recent_articles.title: Kerala fireworks unit blast: CM, Opposition leader express condolences - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** directed the government to provide timely medical care to victims of a fireworks manufacturing unit fire and explosion in Thrissur, Kerala.  **Mr. Vijayan** expressed condolences for the deaths and stated that expert doctors from outside the state may be called upon if needed. The State Disaster Management department allocated ₹50 lakh to meet emergency needs following the accident.

recent_articles.title: CM condemns Nithin Raj’s death as public sentiment galvanises against management of Anjarakandy dental college - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** expressed deep sorrow over the suspected suicide of **Nithin Raj**, a medical student at **Anjarakandy Dental College**, attributing his death to casteism.  He condemned the alleged discrimination and called for justice, emphasizing that Kerala would not forgive those responsible. The incident has sparked public outrage and renewed calls for the implementation of the **Rohith Vemula (Prevention of Discrimination, Exclusion or Injustice) (Right to Education and Dignity) Bill**, proposed by the Karnataka government, to address caste-based discrimination in educational institutions.

recent_articles.title: CM condemns Nithin Raj’s death as public sentiment galvanises against management of Anjarakandy dental college - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** expressed deep sorrow over the suspected suicide of **Nithin Raj**, a medical student at **Anjarakandy Dental College**, attributing his death to casteism on campus.  He condemned the inaction of the **Central government** in addressing the demand for the **Rohith Vemula (Prevention of Discrimination, Exclusion or Injustice) (Right to Education and Dignity) Bill**. The bill aims to prevent caste-based discrimination in educational institutions.
